entry: American multinational software company based in San Jose, California. Founded in December 1982 by John Warnock and Charles Geschke, after they left Xerox PARC to develop and sell the PostScript page description language, Adobe makes flagship products including [[Adobe Photoshop|Photoshop]], Illustrator, Acrobat and the [[PDF|Portable Document Format]]. Its Creative Suite bundle evolved into the subscription-based Creative Cloud. As of 2022, Adobe had more than 26,000 employees worldwide. In 2024, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and the U.S. Department of Justice filed a joint civil lawsuit over its early termination fees for a Creative Cloud plan.

Raster graphics editing software developed by Adobe for Windows and macOS. It was created in 1987 by brothers Thomas and John Knoll. Photoshop edits and composes images in multiple layers, with masks, alpha compositing and several color models, and uses its own PSD and PSB file formats. It is widely used in professional [[Digital art|digital art]], and its name has become a verb, although Adobe disapproves of such use. Since the introduction of Creative Cloud branding in June 2013, it has been licensed by subscription.

German-Austrian [[Schutzstaffel|SS]] officer and convicted war criminal. He participated in the January 20, 1942, Wannsee Conference, which planned the genocidal [[Final Solution]], and he organized the deportation of Jews to extermination camps. By July 1944, 437,000 of Hungary's 725,000 Jews had been deported under his oversight. He settled in Argentina after World War II, and in May 1960 Mossad and Shin Bet agents captured him and brought him to Israel. Found guilty on 15 criminal charges, he was executed by [[Hanging|hanging]] after a trial in [[Jerusalem|Jerusalem]]. [[Hannah Arendt]] coined the phrase "the banality of evil" to describe him.

French statesman and historian, president of France (1871–73). A key figure in the July Revolution of 1830, he served as prime minister in 1836 and 1840. He was first a supporter, then a vocal opponent, of Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte. After [[Napoleon III]] seized power, Thiers was arrested and briefly expelled from France. Following the defeat in the [[Franco-Prussian War]], which he had opposed, he was elected chief executive and negotiated the end of the war. When the [[Paris Commune]] seized power in March 1871, he gave the army orders to suppress it. In August 1871, at the age of 74, the National Assembly named him president of the Republic. He achieved the departure of German soldiers from most of French territory two years ahead of schedule. Opposed by monarchists and left-wing republicans, he resigned on May 24, 1873. Thiers was also a notable popular historian. His ten-volume history of the [[French Revolution]] was published in 1823–1827, and he was elected to the Académie Française in 1834.

Legal process of permanently assuming the parenting of a child in place of the original parents. Legal adoption transfers all rights and responsibilities, along with filiation, to the adoptive parents, and requires societal recognition through legal or religious sanction. The [[Code of Hammurabi]] detailed the rights of adopters and adoptees. In the [[Roman Empire]], adoption strengthened political ties between wealthy families, and many emperors were adopted sons. Medieval bloodline-based nobility largely rejected adoption; [[Common law|English common law]] did not permit it because it contradicted the customary rules of [[Inheritance|inheritance]]. France's [[Napoleonic Code]] made adoption difficult, requiring adopters to be over 50, sterile, at least 15 years older than the adoptee, and to have fostered the adoptee for at least six years. Modern systems, arising in the 20th century, are governed by comprehensive statutes. Regulated adoption in the United States began in [[Massachusetts|Massachusetts]] with the 1851 Adoption of Children Act. About 50,000 children were adopted from U.S. foster care in fiscal year 2023.

Class of words expressing spatial or temporal relations or semantic roles. Adpositions express relations such as in, under, towards and ago, or roles such as of and for. An adposition typically combines with exactly one complement, usually a [[Noun|noun]] phrase, to form an adpositional phrase that modifies or completes another element of a clause. English generally has prepositions, which precede their complement, as in "in England" and "under the table", although ago and notwithstanding are exceptions. Some languages, such as [[Turkic languages|Turkic]], [[Hindi]] and [[Urdu]], use postpositions that follow the complement, and Finnish has both. A circumposition has two parts on either side of the complement. Prepositions, postpositions and circumpositions are collectively called adpositions, though some linguists use preposition for all types regardless of position. The word preposition comes from [[Latin]] prae- ("before") and ponere ("to put").

Endocrine gland located above each [[Kidney|kidney]]. Also called suprarenal glands, each has an outer cortex that produces steroid hormones and an inner medulla. The cortex has three zones. The zona glomerulosa produces mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone, which regulate [[Blood pressure|blood pressure]] and electrolyte balance. The zona fasciculata produces glucocorticoids, including [[Cortisol|cortisol]], which regulate [[Metabolism|metabolism]] and suppress the [[Immune system|immune system]]. The zona reticularis produces androgens. The medulla produces [[Adrenaline|adrenaline]] and other catecholamines, which trigger rapid responses in stress situations. Overproduction of cortisol causes Cushing's syndrome, while insufficient production is associated with Addison's disease. The glands measure approximately 5 cm in length, 3 cm in width and up to 1 cm in thickness, and their combined weight in an adult ranges from 7 to 10 grams.

Hormone and medication, also known as epinephrine. Normally produced by the [[Adrenal gland|adrenal glands]] and a small number of neurons in the medulla oblongata, it plays an essential role in the fight-or-flight response, increasing blood flow to muscles, increasing [[Heart|heart]] output by acting on the SA node, dilating the pupils and raising [[Blood sugar level|blood sugar]]. It binds to alpha and beta receptors. As a medication, it treats anaphylaxis, [[Cardiac arrest|cardiac arrest]] and superficial bleeding, and inhaled adrenaline may ease croup. It can be used for [[Asthma|asthma]] when other treatments are not effective, and it lowers intraocular pressure in open-angle [[Glaucoma|glaucoma]] by increasing outflow of aqueous humor. Common side effects include shakiness, [[Anxiety|anxiety]] and sweating. The adrenal medulla contributes over 90% of circulating adrenaline, and a small number of neurons use it as a [[Neurotransmitter|neurotransmitter]].

Brazilian model. She was a Victoria's Secret Angel from 2000 to 2018 and made her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show debut in 1999, making her the longest-running Victoria's Secret Angel and model. Known for her [[Super Bowl]] and Kia Motors commercials, she was ranked among the top-earning models on [[Forbes|Forbes]]'s list, with earnings of $10.5 million in 2016. She has been a brand ambassador for Desigual, Puma, Maybelline and Chopard.

Northernmost arm of the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]], separating the Italian and Balkan peninsulas. It extends from the Strait of Otranto northwest to the Po Valley and is bordered by [[Albania|Albania]], Bosnia and Herzegovina, [[Croatia|Croatia]], Italy, Montenegro and Slovenia. The sea contains more than 1,300 islands, mostly along its eastern coast. Its southern basin is the deepest, with a maximum depth of 1,233 m (4,045 ft). The Adriatic receives a third of the fresh water flowing into the Mediterranean, so its salinity is lower than the Mediterranean's. More than 7,000 species are identified as native to the sea. In the Middle Ages it was controlled by states including the [[Byzantine Empire]], the Republic of Venice and the [[Ottoman Empire]]. The largest seaport by annual cargo turnover is [[Trieste|Trieste]], and fisheries and tourism are significant to the local economy.

American actor and visual artist. Known for intense, emotionally charged roles, he won two Academy Awards for Best Actor, for *The Pianist* (2002), directed by [[Roman Polanski]], and for *The Brutalist* (2024). At 29, his first win made him the youngest winner in the category. His other films include *The Thin Red Line* and *King Kong*. He earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for his role in the [[HBO]] series *Succession*.

French mathematician with contributions to number theory, celestial mechanics and analysis. Legendre polynomials and the Legendre transformation are named after him. He was the first to officially publish on the [[Least squares|method of least squares]], although [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]] had discovered it before him. He stated the law of quadratic reciprocity in his 1785 work, and Gauss provided the complete proof. His 1794 textbook *Éléments de géométrie* became a standard Euclidean geometry text, widely translated and reprinted. He devised the Legendre symbol to study quadratic residues and advanced integral calculus and elliptic functions, laying groundwork for [[Niels Henrik Abel|Abel]] and [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi|Jacobi]]. He was elected to the Royal Society of London in 1787.

American adult-oriented programming block on [[Cartoon Network|Cartoon Network]]. Launched on September 2, 2001, it broadcasts original comedies, syndicated series and short films, often [[Animation|animated]], [[Parody|parodic]] or satirical, and many programs are experimental, transgressive and surreal. Its Saturday night Toonami block has carried [[Anime|anime]] since May 2012. Adult Swim expanded into prime time in 2008 and to 5:00 p.m. on August 28, 2023.

American animated fantasy television series created by Pendleton Ward for [[Cartoon Network|Cartoon Network]]. Set in the post-apocalyptic Land of Ooo, it follows Finn and his shape-shifting adoptive brother Jake. It is based on Ward's 2007 short film and drew inspiration from [[Dungeons & Dragons|Dungeons & Dragons]] and video games. Produced with hand-drawn animation, the series aired from April 5, 2010, to September 3, 2018. Each episode took roughly eight to nine months to complete. It won eight Primetime Emmy Awards and a Peabody Award.

Picaresque novel by American author [[Mark Twain|Mark Twain]], published in 1884–85. It is a direct sequel to *The Adventures of Tom Sawyer* and is narrated in vernacular first person by Huckleberry Finn, known as Huck. Huck escapes his drunken father and travels down the [[Mississippi River|Mississippi River]] on a raft with Jim, an enslaved man fleeing bondage. Its often scathing [[Satire|satire]] of racism and Southern antebellum society has made it commonly named among the Great American Novels. [[Ernest Hemingway|Ernest Hemingway]] asserted that all modern American literature derives from it. Its frequent use of a racial slur, over 200 times, has led to bans and challenges in schools and libraries since its release.

Word or expression modifying a [[Verb|verb]], an [[Adjective|adjective]], another adverb, a [[Clause|clause]], or a sentence. Adverbs typically express manner, place, time, frequency, degree or level of certainty, answering questions such as how, when, where and to what extent. This adverbial function may be performed by a single word, an adverbial phrase or an adverbial clause. Traditionally one of the parts of speech, the term has become a catch-all for words that do not fit other categories such as [[Noun|noun]] or preposition. [[Sentence (linguistics)|Sentence]] adverbs, such as "fortunately" or "honestly", comment on the whole sentence. English often derives adverbs from adjectives, while [[Romance languages|Romance languages]] use suffixes such as -mente. Adverbs form an open class, so new forms can be created.

Practice and techniques used to bring attention to a product or service. Commercial advertising often seeks increased consumption through [[Brand|branding]], which associates a product name or image with certain qualities in consumers' minds. Direct-response advertising aims for an immediate sale. Non-commercial advertisers include political parties, interest groups, religious organizations and governmental agencies. Worldwide spending on advertising was over US$1 trillion. In 2024, the distribution was 59.4% on digital, 24.9% on TV, 5.2% on out-of-home, 4.5% on [[Radio|radio]], 3.5% on [[Newspaper|newspapers]], 2.2% on [[Magazine|magazines]] and 0.4% on cinema. The earliest documented written advertisement was a [[Papyrus|papyrus]] notice from Egypt, circa 3000 BC, offering a reward for a runaway slave.

Elongated embayment of the Mediterranean Sea between the [[Balkans|Balkans]] and [[Anatolia|Anatolia]]. It covers some 215,000 sq km and connects to the Marmara Sea and the [[Black Sea|Black Sea]] through the Dardanelles and the Bosphorus. The Aegean Islands include the Dodecanese, the Cyclades, the Sporades, the Saronic islands and the North Aegean Islands, as well as [[Crete|Crete]]. The sea was central to [[Ancient Greece|ancient Greek]] civilization. The [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine Empire]] held it against Bulgarian advances, and the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman Empire]] held a presence over the sea for over 500 years until it was replaced by modern Turkey. Crete was a Venetian colony until 1669. The [[Greek War of Independence|Greek War of Independence]] allowed a Greek state on the coast from 1829 onwards. Greece and Turkey dispute the delimitation of territorial waters, airspace and exclusive economic zones, an issue that has had a large effect on relations since the 1970s.

Latin epic poem by [[Virgil|Virgil]], composed 29–19 BC. In twelve books of dactylic hexameter totaling 9,896 lines, it tells how Aeneas, a Trojan who fled the fall of [[Troy|Troy]], travelled to Italy and became the ancestor of the Romans. The first six books follow his wanderings, and the last six describe the Trojans' war against the Latins. Virgil shaped the disconnected tales into a national founding myth that tied Rome to the legends of Troy, explained the [[Punic Wars|Punic Wars]], and legitimized the [[Julio-Claudian dynasty|Julio-Claudian dynasty]] as descendants of Rome's founders. Left unfinished at Virgil's death, the poem was preserved through the intervention of [[Augustus|Augustus]].

Erosion, transportation and deposition of sediment by [[Wind|wind]]. Named after Aeolus, the Greek god of the winds, these processes are important in arid environments with sparse vegetation, lack of soil moisture and abundant unconsolidated sediment, although water is a far more powerful eroding force. Deflation removes fine particles such as silt and clay, while abrasion by windborne sand forms ventifacts and yardangs. Particles smaller than 0.2 mm are carried in suspension and form loess; the thickest known deposit, 335 m, lies on [[China|China]]'s Loess Plateau. Sand grains of 0.2–2 mm move by saltation, bouncing in hops up to 1 cm high. Deposition forms sand sheets and [[Dune|dunes]], which need a minimum height of 30 cm to maintain their form. Common types include barchans and transverse dunes.

Transfer of fuel from one aircraft to another while both are in flight. The two main systems are probe-and-drogue, which is simpler to adapt to existing aircraft, and the flying boom, which transfers fuel faster but requires a dedicated boom operator. Refueling lets the receiver stay airborne longer, extending its range or loiter time, and allows a takeoff with a greater payload. Since the [[Vietnam War|Vietnam War]], it has been extensively used in large-scale military operations. There are no regular civilian in-flight refueling activities.

Military combat involving aircraft and other flying machines. It includes [[Bomber|bombers]] attacking enemy installations, [[Fighter aircraft|fighter aircraft]] contesting control of airspace, attack aircraft providing close air support, and helicopters or gliders carrying airborne forces. Transport aircraft move cargo and personnel, and [[Aerial refueling|aerial refueling]] tankers extend operating time or range. Early forms included [[Airship|airships]] for bombing cities and balloons carrying artillery observers. Aerial warfare emerged in [[World War I|World War I]] for reconnaissance and expanded into strategic bombing in [[World War II|World War II]]. Postwar jet propulsion, radar and guided munitions shifted tactics toward missiles and precision strikes. In the 1991 Gulf War, coalition air forces neutralized Iraqi defenses before ground operations. Modern systems include missiles and [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|unmanned aerial vehicles]], and surface forces respond to enemy air activity with [[Anti-aircraft warfare|anti-aircraft warfare]].

Branch of dynamics concerned with the motion of air, particularly when affected by a solid object. The term comes from [[Ancient Greek|Ancient Greek]] words for air and dynamics. Its principles, developed through mathematical analysis, empirical approximation, wind tunnel experimentation and [[Computer simulation|computer simulations]], form a basis for heavier-than-air flight and other technologies. Systematic development accelerated in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, culminating in the [[Wright brothers|Wright brothers]]' first powered flight in 1903. Four forces act on an aircraft: [[Lift (force)|lift]], [[Drag (physics)|drag]], thrust and weight, which must balance for sustained flight. [[Bernoulli's principle|Bernoulli's principle]] explains how variations in air speed create pressure differences that produce lift. Subfields include incompressible aerodynamics for low-speed flows and compressible aerodynamics for high-speed regimes, where shock waves become critical.

American rock band formed in [[Boston|Boston]] in 1970. Its blues-based hard rock has also incorporated pop rock, heavy metal, glam metal and rhythm and blues, and influenced many later rock artists. The band is the best-selling American hard rock band of all time, with more than 150 million records sold worldwide. Its first number-one hit was "I Don't Want to Miss a Thing" in 1998. Aerosmith was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame|Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2001. It retired from touring in 2024.

[[Suspension (chemistry)|Suspension]] of fine solid particles or liquid droplets in air or another gas. Under ISO 16972, aerosol particles broadly have falling velocities less than 0.25 m/s, and their diameters are typically less than 10 μm. The scientific term refers to the particles together with the gas, not the particulate matter alone. Natural aerosols include sea spray, windblown dust, volcanic emissions, and [[Fog|fog]] and [[Cloud|clouds]]. Anthropogenic aerosols include [[Combustion|combustion]] smoke such as [[Cigarette|cigarette smoke]] and secondary aerosols formed by chemical reactions, such as photochemical smog. In common usage, the term refers to a spray-can dispensing system. Prolonged, repeated exposure raises the risk of cardiorespiratory death and chronic respiratory illness.
